import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Opaque forest problem

An *opaque set* (or *barrier*, *opaque cover*) for a planar set $K$ is a set $B$ in the plane
that meets every line meeting $K$. The opaque forest problem asks for the shortest opaque set
of a given shape, where the length of an arbitrary set is its one-dimensional Hausdorff
measure $\mathcal{H}^1$. The barrier is unrestricted in location (it may lie outside $K$) and
need not be connected.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Opaque forest problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opaque_forest_problem)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [DJP14] Dumitrescu, A., Jiang, M., Pach, J., _Opaque sets_. Algorithmica 69 (2014), 315–334.
  [arXiv:1005.2218](https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.2218)
- [DJ14] Dumitrescu, A., Jiang, M., _The opaque square_. Proc. 30th Annual Symposium on
  Computational Geometry (SoCG'14). [arXiv:1311.3323](https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.3323)
- [PBTW12] Provan, J. S., Brazil, M., Thomas, D. A., Weng, J. F., _Minimum opaque covers for
  polygonal regions_. [arXiv:1210.8139](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.8139)
- [Iz16] Izumi, T., _Improving the lower bound on opaque sets for equilateral triangle_.
  Discrete Applied Mathematics 213 (2016), 130–138.
-/

open scoped ENNReal

blocks.docstring:
A set `B` in the plane is an *opaque set* (or *barrier*) for the set `K` if every line in the
plane that meets `K` also meets `B`. A line is an affine subspace of `ℝ²` whose direction is
one-dimensional. No restriction is placed on `B`: it may lie outside `K` and need not be
connected.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Erdos209.IsLine (local to another problem file, not importable) and line[ℝ, p, q] with p ≠ q; the finrank condition was inlined instead.
justification.name: OpaqueForestProblem.IsOpaqueSet
justification.why_needed: No notion of 'opaque set / barrier' (a set meeting every line that meets K) exists in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib. Defined as: for every affine subspace L of ℝ² with Module.finrank ℝ L.direction = 1 (exactly the lines; ⊥ and points have finrank 0, the plane has finrank 2), (K ∩ L).Nonempty → (B ∩ L).Nonempty.

blocks.name: IsOpaqueSet
blocks.text:
/--
A set `B` in the plane is an *opaque set* (or *barrier*) for the set `K` if every line in the
plane that meets `K` also meets `B`. A line is an affine subspace of `ℝ²` whose direction is
one-dimensional. No restriction is placed on `B`: it may lie outside `K` and need not be
connected.
-/
def IsOpaqueSet (K B : Set ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∀ L : AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ², Module.finrank ℝ L.direction = 1 →
    (K ∩ L).Nonempty → (B ∩ L).Nonempty

noncomputable def opaqueLengths (K : Set ℝ²) : Set ℝ≥0∞ :=
  μH[1] '' {B | IsOpaqueSet K B}

@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem IsOpaqueSet.mono {K B B' : Set ℝ²} (h : IsOpaqueSet K B) (hB : B ⊆ B') :
    IsOpaqueSet K B' :=
  fun L hL hK => (h L hL hK).mono (Set.inter_subset_inter_left _ hB)

@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem :
    IsGLB (opaqueLengths unitSquare) (ENNReal.ofReal (√2 + √6 / 2)) := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Opaque forest problem for the unit square.**
The shortest known opaque set for the unit square is the two-component forest of Jones and
Poirier: the minimum Steiner tree of three of the corners of the square together with the
segment from the fourth corner to the centre. It has length
$\sqrt{2} + \tfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{6} \approx 2.639$ and is conjectured to be optimal [DJP14, DJ14].
The conjecture: the infimum of the lengths ($\mathcal{H}^1$-measures) of all opaque sets for the
unit square equals $\sqrt{2} + \tfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{6}$. The barrier is unrestricted in location
and need not be connected. This is stated as an infimum rather than an attained minimum, since
the existence of a shortest opaque set is itself open.

@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem.variants.minimizer_exists :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ K : Set ℝ², IsCompact K → Convex ℝ K → (interior K).Nonempty →
      ∃ B, IsOpaqueSet K B ∧ ∀ B', IsOpaqueSet K B' → μH[1] B ≤ μH[1] B' := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Existence of a shortest opaque set.**
Does every convex body $K$ in the plane (a compact convex set with nonempty interior) have a
shortest opaque set? That is, is there an opaque set for $K$ whose length
($\mathcal{H}^1$-measure) is at most the length of every other opaque set for $K$? The
alternative is that the lengths of the opaque sets for $K$ approach their infimum without ever
reaching it. The opaque sets range over arbitrary subsets of the plane and are unrestricted in
location. The nonempty interior excludes degenerate bodies (points and segments).
blocks.name: opaque_forest_problem.variants.minimizer_exists

blocks.code:
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem.variants.graphical_conjecture (V : Finset ℝ²)
    (hV : (interior (convexHull ℝ (V : Set ℝ²))).Nonempty) :
    ∃ B, IsFiniteUnionOfSegments B ∧ IsOpaqueSet (convexHull ℝ (V : Set ℝ²)) B ∧
      ∀ B', IsOpaqueSet (convexHull ℝ (V : Set ℝ²)) B' → μH[1] B ≤ μH[1] B' := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**The Graphical Conjecture** of Provan, Brazil, Thomas and Weng [PBTW12].
Every convex polygon (the convex hull of finitely many points of the plane, with nonempty
interior) has a shortest opaque set that is *graphical*, i.e. a finite union of line segments
(an opaque forest). In other words, some finite union of line segments is an opaque set for the
polygon whose length ($\mathcal{H}^1$-measure) is at most the length of every other opaque set
for the polygon. In particular every convex polygon has a shortest opaque set.
Following [PBTW12], no acyclicity condition is imposed on the union of segments.
blocks.name: opaque_forest_problem.variants.graphical_conjecture
blocks.text:
/--
**The Graphical Conjecture** of Provan, Brazil, Thomas and Weng [PBTW12].
Every convex polygon (the convex hull of finitely many points of the plane, with nonempty
interior) has a shortest opaque set that is *graphical*, i.e. a finite union of line segments
(an opaque forest). In other words, some finite union of line segments is an opaque set for the
polygon whose length ($\mathcal{H}^1$-measure) is at most the length of every other opaque set
for the polygon. In particular every convex polygon has a shortest opaque set.
Following [PBTW12], no acyclicity condition is imposed on the union of segments.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem.variants.graphical_conjecture (V : Finset ℝ²)
    (hV : (interior (convexHull ℝ (V : Set ℝ²))).Nonempty) :
    ∃ B, IsFiniteUnionOfSegments B ∧ IsOpaqueSet (convexHull ℝ (V : Set ℝ²)) B ∧
      ∀ B', IsOpaqueSet (convexHull ℝ (V : Set ℝ²)) B' → μH[1] B ≤ μH[1] B' := by
  sorry

blocks.code:
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem.variants.equilateral_triangle (a b c : ℝ²)
    (hab : dist a b = 1) (hbc : dist b c = 1) (hca : dist c a = 1) :
    IsGLB (opaqueLengths (convexHull ℝ {a, b, c})) (ENNReal.ofReal √3) := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Opaque sets for the equilateral triangle.**
The shortest connected opaque set for a triangle is its minimum Steiner tree; for an
equilateral triangle of side length $1$ this tree consists of the three segments from the
vertices to the centre and has length $\sqrt{3}$. Without assuming connectivity, the
optimality of the Steiner tree has not been demonstrated [DJP14, PBTW12, Iz16]: the conjecture
is that the infimum of the lengths ($\mathcal{H}^1$-measures) of all opaque sets for an
equilateral triangle of side length $1$ equals $\sqrt{3}$. The barrier is unrestricted in
location and need not be connected.
blocks.name: opaque_forest_problem.variants.equilateral_triangle

claims.decomposer_note: Candidate asserted by the cited papers ("conjectured to be optimal"): the infimum of the 1-dimensional Hausdorff measure (length) over all opaque sets of the unit square is √2 + √6/2 (the Jones/Poirier two-component forest); the barrier is unrestricted in location and need not be connected, and since any opaque set can be approximated in length by opaque forests the infimum may be taken over forests of segments or over general sets with H^1 measure — state it as an IsGLB/infimum equality rather than an attained minimum, since existence of a minimizer is itself open.
claims.reviewer_why: IsGLB (opaqueLengths unitSquare) (ofReal (√2+√6/2)) over ALL opaque sets (arbitrary subsets of ℝ², μH[1], unrestricted location, no connectivity), exactly the infimum form the notes require; matches DJP14/DJ14 'conjectured to be optimal' for arbitrary (disconnected) barriers and PBTW's H^1 framing. All 8 candidates agree in substance; c05 chosen for clean definitions and proved API lemmas. Docstring trimmed by me.

claims.decomposer_note: Provan–Brazil–Thomas–Weng's Graphical Conjecture: for every convex polygon there is a finite union of line segments (an opaque forest) that is an opaque set of minimum length; this implies existence of a minimizer for polygons, and one must decide whether 'forest' requires the union to be acyclic (the sources' 'graphical' just means finitely many segments).
claims.reviewer_why: ∀ Finset V with nonempty-interior hull, ∃ B finite union of closed segments, opaque for the hull, with length ≤ every opaque set (global minimum, not just among forests). Existential reading of PBTW's 'a minimum OC is always graphical' (universal reading is trivially false via null-set additions and vacuous without existence), matching Wikipedia's 'has an opaque forest as its shortest opaque set'. Acyclicity not imposed, following PBTW's 'graphical'; a shortest finite segment union is automatically acyclic, so equivalent. c01's IsConvexPolygon formulation is also fine but Finset hull is simpler.

context:
In discrete geometry, an opaque set is a system of curves or other set in the plane that blocks all lines of sight across a polygon, circle, or other shape. Opaque sets have also been called barriers, beam detectors, opaque covers, or (in cases where they have the form of a forest of line segments or other curves) opaque forests. Opaque sets were introduced by Stefan Mazurkiewicz in 1916, and the problem of minimizing their total length was posed by Frederick Bagemihl in 1959.
For instance, visibility through a unit square can be blocked by its four boundary edges, with length 4, but a shorter opaque forest blocks visibility across the square with length ${\sqrt {2}}+{\tfrac {1}{2}}{\sqrt {6}}\approx 2.639$. It is unproven whether this is the shortest possible opaque set for the square, and for most other shapes this problem similarly remains unsolved. The shortest opaque set for any bounded convex set in the plane has length at most the perimeter of the set, and at least half the perimeter. For the square, a slightly stronger lower bound than half the perimeter is known. Another convex set whose opaque sets are commonly studied is the unit circle, for which the shortest connected opaque set has length $2+\pi$. Without the assumption of connectivity, the shortest opaque set for the circle has length at least $\pi$ and at most $4.7998$.

decomposition_objections.text: Minor: for the equilateral_triangle slot, Provan–Brazil–Thomas–Weng (arXiv:1210.8139, end of Sect. 5 and Sect. 6) do explicitly conjecture that the minimum (graphical) opaque cover of an arbitrary triangle is its minimum Steiner tree, so the arbitrary-triangle version is asserted as a conjecture in the primary literature; the table's restriction to the unit equilateral triangle (infimum √3) was followed as instructed. Also, the table's wording 'opaque forest' for the graphical_conjecture slot differs slightly from Provan et al.'s 'graphical' (no acyclicity); the two are equivalent for existence of a minimizer, as recorded in modeling_decisions.

- [DJP14] Dumitrescu, A., Jiang, M., Pach, J., _Opaque sets_. Algorithmica 69 (2014), 315–334.
  [arXiv:1005.2218](https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.2218)
- [DJ14] Dumitrescu, A., Jiang, M., _The opaque square_. Proc. 30th Annual Symposium on
  Computational Geometry (SoCG'14). [arXiv:1311.3323](https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.3323)
- [PBTW12] Provan, J. S., Brazil, M., Thomas, D. A., Weng, J. F., _Minimum opaque covers for
  polygonal regions_. [arXiv:1210.8139](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.8139)
- [Iz16] Izumi, T., _Improving the lower bound on opaque sets for equilateral triangle_.
  Discrete Applied Mathematics 213 (2016), 130–138.
-/

open EuclideanGeometry MeasureTheory
open scoped ENNReal

namespace OpaqueForestProblem

/--
A set `B` in the plane is an *opaque set* (or *barrier*) for the set `K` if every line in the
plane that meets `K` also meets `B`. A line is an affine subspace of `ℝ²` whose direction is
one-dimensional. No restriction is placed on `B`: it may lie outside `K` and need not be
connected.
-/
def IsOpaqueSet (K B : Set ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∀ L : AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ², Module.finrank ℝ L.direction = 1 →
    (K ∩ L).Nonempty → (B ∩ L).Nonempty

/--
The set of lengths of all opaque sets for `K`, where the length of an arbitrary set is its
one-dimensional Hausdorff measure $\mathcal{H}^1$ (which agrees with the usual length for line
segments and rectifiable curves).
-/
noncomputable def opaqueLengths (K : Set ℝ²) : Set ℝ≥0∞ :=
  μH[1] '' {B | IsOpaqueSet K B}

/-- A set is a *finite union of line segments* if it is the union of finitely many (closed)
line segments. Following [PBTW12], such opaque sets are called *graphical*. -/
def IsFiniteUnionOfSegments (B : Set ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Finset (ℝ² × ℝ²), B = ⋃ e ∈ S, segment ℝ e.1 e.2

/-- The unit square $[0, 1]^2$, as the convex hull of its four corners. -/
def unitSquare : Set ℝ² :=
  convexHull ℝ {!₂[0, 0], !₂[1, 0], !₂[0, 1], !₂[1, 1]}

/-- Every set is an opaque set for itself. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem isOpaqueSet_self (K : Set ℝ²) : IsOpaqueSet K K :=
  fun _ _ h => h

/-- Enlarging an opaque set keeps it opaque. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem IsOpaqueSet.mono {K B B' : Set ℝ²} (h : IsOpaqueSet K B) (hB : B ⊆ B') :
    IsOpaqueSet K B' :=
  fun L hL hK => (h L hL hK).mono (Set.inter_subset_inter_left _ hB)

/-- An opaque set for `K` is an opaque set for every subset of `K`. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem IsOpaqueSet.anti {K K' B : Set ℝ²} (h : IsOpaqueSet K B) (hK : K' ⊆ K) :
    IsOpaqueSet K' B :=
  fun L hL hK' => h L hL (hK'.mono (Set.inter_subset_inter_left _ hK))

/-- The length of `K` itself belongs to the set of lengths of opaque sets for `K`. -/
@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem hausdorffMeasure_mem_opaqueLengths (K : Set ℝ²) : μH[1] K ∈ opaqueLengths K :=
  ⟨K, isOpaqueSet_self K, rfl⟩

/-- A single line segment is a finite union of line segments. -/
@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem isFiniteUnionOfSegments_segment (p q : ℝ²) :
    IsFiniteUnionOfSegments (segment ℝ p q) :=
  ⟨{(p, q)}, by simp⟩

/-- The corner `(1, 1)` lies in the unit square. -/
@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem mem_unitSquare : !₂[1, 1] ∈ unitSquare :=
  subset_convexHull ℝ _ (by simp)

/--
**Opaque forest problem for the unit square.**
The shortest known opaque set for the unit square is the two-component forest of Jones and
Poirier: the minimum Steiner tree of three of the corners of the square together with the
segment from the fourth corner to the centre. It has length
$\sqrt{2} + \tfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{6} \approx 2.639$ and is conjectured to be optimal [DJP14, DJ14].
The conjecture: the infimum of the lengths ($\mathcal{H}^1$-measures) of all opaque sets for the
unit square equals $\sqrt{2} + \tfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{6}$. The barrier is unrestricted in location
and need not be connected. This is stated as an infimum rather than an attained minimum, since
the existence of a shortest opaque set is itself open.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem :
    IsGLB (opaqueLengths unitSquare) (ENNReal.ofReal (√2 + √6 / 2)) := by
  sorry

/--
**Existence of a shortest opaque set.**
Does every convex body $K$ in the plane (a compact convex set with nonempty interior) have a
shortest opaque set? That is, is there an opaque set for $K$ whose length
($\mathcal{H}^1$-measure) is at most the length of every other opaque set for $K$? The
alternative is that the lengths of the opaque sets for $K$ approach their infimum without ever
reaching it. The opaque sets range over arbitrary subsets of the plane and are unrestricted in
location. The nonempty interior excludes degenerate bodies (points and segments).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem.variants.minimizer_exists :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ K : Set ℝ², IsCompact K → Convex ℝ K → (interior K).Nonempty →
      ∃ B, IsOpaqueSet K B ∧ ∀ B', IsOpaqueSet K B' → μH[1] B ≤ μH[1] B' := by
  sorry

/--
**The Graphical Conjecture** of Provan, Brazil, Thomas and Weng [PBTW12].
Every convex polygon (the convex hull of finitely many points of the plane, with nonempty
interior) has a shortest opaque set that is *graphical*, i.e. a finite union of line segments
(an opaque forest). In other words, some finite union of line segments is an opaque set for the
polygon whose length ($\mathcal{H}^1$-measure) is at most the length of every other opaque set
for the polygon. In particular every convex polygon has a shortest opaque set.
Following [PBTW12], no acyclicity condition is imposed on the union of segments.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem.variants.graphical_conjecture (V : Finset ℝ²)
    (hV : (interior (convexHull ℝ (V : Set ℝ²))).Nonempty) :
    ∃ B, IsFiniteUnionOfSegments B ∧ IsOpaqueSet (convexHull ℝ (V : Set ℝ²)) B ∧
      ∀ B', IsOpaqueSet (convexHull ℝ (V : Set ℝ²)) B' → μH[1] B ≤ μH[1] B' := by
  sorry

/--
**Opaque sets for the equilateral triangle.**
The shortest connected opaque set for a triangle is its minimum Steiner tree; for an
equilateral triangle of side length $1$ this tree consists of the three segments from the
vertices to the centre and has length $\sqrt{3}$. Without assuming connectivity, the
optimality of the Steiner tree has not been demonstrated [DJP14, PBTW12, Iz16]: the conjecture
is that the infimum of the lengths ($\mathcal{H}^1$-measures) of all opaque sets for an
equilateral triangle of side length $1$ equals $\sqrt{3}$. The barrier is unrestricted in
location and need not be connected.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem.variants.equilateral_triangle (a b c : ℝ²)
    (hab : dist a b = 1) (hbc : dist b c = 1) (hca : dist c a = 1) :
    IsGLB (opaqueLengths (convexHull ℝ {a, b, c})) (ENNReal.ofReal √3) := by
  sorry

end OpaqueForestProblem

items: Lines are modelled as affine subspaces L of ℝ² = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) with Module.finrank ℝ L.direction = 1; checked that this excludes ⊥ (direction ⊥, finrank 0).

Length is Mathlib's μH[1] on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) (Euclidean, not sup, metric); Mathlib's hausdorffMeasure is the unnormalized diam-cover definition, identical to the λ₁ used by Provan et al., and agrees with Euclidean length on segments (μH[1] = volume on ℝ plus isometry invariance). Values live in ℝ≥0∞, so the target constants are written ENNReal.ofReal (√2 + √6 / 2) and ENNReal.ofReal √3.

Slot 1 and slot 4 are stated as IsGLB (infimum) over the lengths of ALL opaque sets (arbitrary subsets of the plane, unrestricted in location, not necessarily connected), per the notes; since every opaque set can be approximated in length by opaque forests, taking the infimum over forests would give the same value.

Slot 1 uses the concrete unit square [0,1]^2 (as convex hull of its corners); slot 4 quantifies over all equilateral triangles of side 1 (pairwise distances 1). Both are isometry-invariant so either style is faithful; the closed square has the same opaque sets as its boundary.

Slot 2: 'convex set' is read as 'convex body' (IsCompact, Convex ℝ, nonempty interior), following the cited papers and the notes. Degenerate compact convex sets (point, segment, empty) and unbounded convex sets trivially have attained minima, so this restriction does not change the mathematical content. Mathlib's ConvexBody structure was not used because it does not require nonempty interior; explicit hypotheses were used instead.

Slot 3: 'opaque forest' is modelled as a finite union of closed line segments (Provan et al.'s 'graphical'), without an explicit acyclicity requirement. A minimum-length finite union of segments cannot contain a cycle (removing the relative interior of an edge of a simple cycle keeps every transversal line blocked and strictly shortens the set), so 'exists a graphical minimizer' and 'exists a forest minimizer' are equivalent statements. The statement is the existential reading (there IS a graphical shortest opaque set), matching Wikipedia and the notes; the reading 'every minimizer is graphical' would be literally false (adding a countable set of points to a minimizer keeps it a minimizer).
Slot 3: 'convex polygon' is convexHull ℝ V for a Finset V with nonempty interior; V may contain non-vertex points, which does not change the polygon.
Copyright year 2026 matches the most recent files in the repository; AMS 52 (convex and discrete geometry) is used for all statements.

reviewer_notes:
All eight candidates compiled and converged on the same content; differences are cosmetic (line representation via affineSpan/finrank/parametrization, coordinate vs convex-hull square, IsGLB vs ⨅, IsLeast vs explicit ≤). Final file is based on c05 with docstrings tightened (removed review-style justification text per AGENTS.md). Compiles with only 'declaration uses sorry' warnings.

Ambiguities a human should know: (1) The primary sources differ in barrier class: DJP14/DJ14 restrict barriers to countable unions of rectifiable arcs, whereas PBTW12 (and the Wikipedia Definitions section) allow arbitrary sets measured by H^1. The file follows PBTW/Wikipedia and the decomposition notes (arbitrary sets). DJP Lemma 1 only shows rectifiable barriers can be approximated by (countable) segment barriers; Wikipedia's unconditional 'every opaque set can be approximated by an opaque forest' is not a proven statement I could locate for non-rectifiable sets. Under the Wikipedia/PBTW framing the statements are nonetheless exactly the conjectures as posed. (2) 'Convex set' in minimizer_exists is read as compact convex with nonempty interior (convex body), per the notes; degenerate and unbounded convex sets trivially have minimizers in ℝ≥0∞, so this restriction does not change the mathematical content. (3) 'Opaque forest' in the Graphical Conjecture is modeled as a finite union of closed segments without acyclicity (PBTW's 'graphical'); the existential reading is used. (4) Equilateral-triangle slot restricted to unit side (√3) per the table; several candidates correctly noted PBTW also conjecture the MST for arbitrary triangles (as 'minimum graphical OC'), which was not formalized as the table did not request it. Dropped items ('most other shapes', circle bounds) were not formalized as instructed. No candidate omitted any slot; no omission reasons to weigh.
